message.content: I placed a single buy order for 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75, which filled at $222.75 — a total of roughly $9,801, comfortably inside the $10,000-per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, with the limit price set $0.03 above the quoted ask of $222.72 so it was close to market. My decision rested on Apple's FY2024 (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024) results from the 10-K: revenue of $391.0B (up 2% year over year), operating income of $123.2B, operating cash flow of $118.3B, net income of $93.7B and diluted EPS of $6.08 — with the profit decline from FY2023's $97.0B explained by a disclosed one-time $10.2B net State Aid tax charge that lifted the effective tax rate to 24.1%, rather than by any operating deterioration (gross margin actually improved to 46.2%, led by Services revenue of $96.2B, up 13%). Those figures, plus a very strong liquidity position, justified a modest position; the offsetting concerns I weighed were the 8% decline in Greater China net sales and antitrust/regulatory exposure (DOJ suit, EU DMA proceedings). The account held $50,000 cash and 100 MSFT shares, no money was moved out, and the position remains the only AAPL holding.
